newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita posts healthy profit on yen, good sales.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita posts healthy profit on yen, good sales.

text.p: Japanese consumer electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co unveiled a healthy group annual profit on Thursday, helped by robust sales of high-tech products and the weak yen.

Matsushita, which sells under the National and Panasonic brands, posted a group net profit of 137.85 billion yen ($1.19 billion) in the 1996/97 business year, which ended in March, after a loss of 56.87 billion yen ($494 million) in the previous year.
Clearly on the road to recovery from a consumer electronics slump in the early 1990s, Matsushita also enjoyed a hefty rise in its parent profits.

The Osaka-based company said its current profit jumped nearly 40 percent to 143.31 billion yen ($1.24 billion) last business year, and predicted profits would grow further to 155 billion yen ($1.34 billion) this year. Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.

Analysts said the firm's strategy of shifting towards high-tech goods from traditional consumer appliances had begun to bear fruit, as it looks set for strong sales of cellular phones, batteries and computer-related goods.

Along with other Japanese exporters such as Sony Corp, Matsushita is a major beneficiary of the weak yen, which its makes goods more price-competitive overseas. The dollar averaged around 113 yen in 1996/97 against 97 yen the year before. ($1=115 yen)
